newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-STIMPSON, BEAL ENJOY FIELD DAY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-STIMPSON, BEAL ENJOY FIELD DAY.

text.p: Tim Stimpson's haul of 26 points and a hat-trick of tries from Nick Beal helped the British Lions to a comfortable 51-22 win over the Emerging Springboks in their final match before Saturday's first test.
Full-back Stimpson, battling to dislodge Neil Jenkins from the test starting line-up, gave the selectors something to think about with a try and nine successful kicks out of 11 attempts at goal.

Beal's tries all came in the second-half after the Lions had led by just a point at the interval, ensuring the touring team will go into the Cape Town test with a record of seven wins from eight matches.
They had raced into a 13-0 lead after just 11 minutes but were pegged back by the aspiring Springboks who scored two tries through flanker Warren Brosnihan and replacement back Marius Goosen.
The first of winger Beal's three tries came within three minutes of the restart and set the tone for a dominant Lions display in the second period.
Their slick passing put Beal in for a further two tries while Stimpson and fly-half Mike Catt both profited from quickly-taken tap penalties close to the home side's line to score simple tries.
The Emerging Springboks -- seven of whom toured the United Kingdom with the South Africa A side at the end of 1996 -- were limited to one further try after the interval through Paul Treu.

Emerging Springboks - 15-MJ Smith (Kaya Malotana, 61); 14-Deon Kayser, 13-Percival Montgomery, 12-McNeil Hendricks, 11-Paul Treu; 10-Louis van Rensburg (Marius Goosen, 20), 9-Jopie Adlam (Katt Myburgh, 15); 8-Jaco Coetzee, 7-Phillip Smit, 6-Warren Bronihan, 5-Braam Els, 4-Ryno Opperman, 3-Neil du Toit, 2-Dale Santon (captain) 1-Robbie Kempson (Lourens Campher, 64).

British Lions - 15-Tim Stimpson; 14-John Bentley, 13-Allan Bateman, 12-Will Greenwood, 11-Nick Beal; 10-Mike Catt, 9-Austin Healey; 8-Tony Diprose, 7-Neil Back, 6-Rob Wainwright, 5-Jeremy Davidson, 4-Nigel Redman, 3-Jason Leonard, 2-Mark Regan, 1-Graham Rowntree.
